meta.headline: Has a leap second ever been taken away?
meta.seoTitle: Leap Seconds: Added Every Time, Never Removed

dek.text: The official leap-second record answers it directly: every adjustment since 1972 has added a second, and none has ever been taken away.

assertions.text: Every leap second since UTC began in 1972 has added a second to civil time; none has ever been taken away.

description.text: Every leap second recorded since 1972 has added a second to civil time; none has ever been taken away, according to the official record.

assertions.text: Every leap second since UTC began in 1972 has added a second to civil time; none has ever been taken away.

sections.name: answer
sections.heading: Only ever added, never taken away

sentences.text: The International Earth Rotation and Reference Systems Service keeps the one official table of every adjustment made to civil time since the current standard began in 1972.

assertions.text: The IERS table of TAI-UTC records every adjustment to civil time since 1 January 1972.

sentences.text: Its 28 entries move only one way, from 10 seconds in 1972 to 37 seconds in 2017, each one second more than the last.

assertions.text: The IERS table of TAI-UTC lists 28 values from 10 s on 1 January 1972 to 37 s on 1 January 2017, each exactly one second larger than the one before.

sentences.text: So the record is clear: a leap second has only ever been added, never taken away.

assertions.text: Every one of the 27 steps in the IERS table added a second to civil time; none subtracted one.

blocks.caption: The TAI-UTC value at the record's first and latest entries, with the steps between them, all moving the same direction.
